canonical_order: sorted(article_id) — identical to embeddings and positions
index_invariant: atlas tile i, colours.bin row i, positions.bin point i and article_ids.json[i] are the SAME article. Asserted in tests.

desktop.uv_rule: layer = i // tiles_per_sheet; within = i % tiles_per_sheet; u = (within % tiles_per_side) / tiles_per_side; v = (within // tiles_per_side) / tiles_per_side

mobile.uv_rule: layer = i // tiles_per_sheet; within = i % tiles_per_sheet; u = (within % tiles_per_side) / tiles_per_side; v = (within // tiles_per_side) / tiles_per_side

signal_colour.method: Design brief (§12.2) sets the admissible set — electric cyan or hot magenta. Catalogue hue occupancy picks between them. Taste bounds the search; data chooses inside it.
signal_colour.why_not_unconstrained: The globally emptiest bin is acid green, which §12.2 lists among the deliberately avoided treatments. Recorded rather than silently discarded.

format.deviation_from_plan: PLAN.md §8 specified KTX2/ETC1S, which stays compressed in VRAM. The basisu toolchain is absent, so WebP is used: browser-native, no toolchain, ~1MB/sheet over the wire. Cost is GPU memory — WebP decodes to uncompressed RGBA (~268MB for 4 desktop sheets vs ~32MB for ETC1S). Fine on unified-memory Apple Silicon and desktop GPUs; the mobile variant is a single 32px sheet at 3k instances for that reason. Moving to KTX2 is a toolchain install, not a redesign.
